claim: Formography can be used only with explicit acknowledgment of its 2021 STS cognate
evidence_needed: exact-term sources; publication-status review; explicit contrast
falsification_signal: prior use owns the same cross-domain method or creates unavoidable confusion

claim: The method is distinguishable from ordinary concept mapping
evidence_needed: contract comparison; representative artifacts; independent coding
falsification_signal: concept-map conventions reproduce the complete output without loss

claim: The method is distinguishable from knowledge graphs and semantic networks
evidence_needed: semantics and governance comparison; graph implementation test
falsification_signal: difference is only editorial styling over an ordinary graph

claim: The method is distinguishable from formal ontology engineering
evidence_needed: authority; axiom; open-world; inference; versioning comparison
falsification_signal: Formography requires ontology commitments it claims to avoid

claim: Forms factors relations frames and projections can be coded consistently
evidence_needed: coding manual; multiple coders; disagreement log
falsification_signal: core object boundaries remain unstable across cases

claim: The method is useful across domains without one domain owning the vocabulary
evidence_needed: physical organizational mathematical and interpretive cases
falsification_signal: core terms change meaning silently between domains

claim: Typed relation and loss custody create inspectable value beyond a glossary
evidence_needed: artifact comparison; practitioner tasks; error analysis
falsification_signal: users receive no consequential distinction or trace

claim: The method can be implemented independently of Factorium
evidence_needed: second implementation or manual packet reproduction
falsification_signal: Factorium-specific conventions are required but undeclared

claim: Formarium is a natural reference consequence of the method
evidence_needed: publication architecture; corpus rules; reader evaluation
falsification_signal: collection identity drives the method rather than following it

claim: A field-level name simplifies explanation and research
evidence_needed: terminology test; paper review; onboarding comparison
falsification_signal: new vocabulary increases explanation cost or confusion

claim: Current Factorium artifacts are evidence cases rather than proof of a field
falsification_signal: local artifacts are reported as external validation

claim: Novelty must attach to the exact method contract rather than factor or graph primitives
falsification_signal: paper claims invention of established primitives

claim: A Structure Atlas can provide a useful reader projection without becoming the canonical collection
evidence_needed: projection contract; comparative layouts; reader tasks
falsification_signal: atlas selection silently replaces source records or adds no value beyond an index
